task.description: WTI Crude Oil continuous front-month futures Close price (yfinance symbol: CL=F), projected 5, 10, and 21 trading days ahead.

spec.description: Prospective/out-of-sample evaluation period in 2026 for daily WTI crude oil. Evaluates selected contender models on 8 weekly origins during the early 2026 geopolitical price shock to measure adaptive real-time forecasting performance.

metadata.agent_rationale: Under the current normal volatility regime (32.4% annualized volatility as of Jan 30, 2026), the WTI crude oil market is balancing short-term geopolitical tensions and OPEC+ production pauses with long-term structural oversupply. Following our forecasting strategy, we narrowed the baseline ARIMA intervals across all horizons (by 30%, 45%, and 50% for horizons 5, 10, and 21 business days, respectively) to resolve systematic overestimation of uncertainty. We also adjusted the 21-day point forecast downward by $1.75 to correct for the baseline's long-horizon over-forecasting bias in medium volatility regimes during bearish structural cycles.
metadata.horizon_rationale: Applied a 30% narrowing of the 80% prediction interval based on systematic baseline uncertainty overestimation. Point forecast is kept at the ARIMA baseline of 65.35 as the normal volatility regime (32.4%) does not warrant short-term bias adjustment, aligning with near-term geopolitical risk premiums and OPEC+ continuing its production cuts pause.

metadata.agent_rationale: Forecast as of 2026-02-09. Classified current volatility regime as elevated (rolling annualised volatility of 36.4%). Applied strategic interval narrowing calibration to correct the systematic over-dispersion of the AutoARIMA baseline's 80% prediction intervals, narrowing them by 30%, 45%, and 50% for 5-bd, 10-bd, and 21-bd horizons respectively to align coverage with the target 80% level. Retained baseline point forecasts (63.84, 63.98, 63.70) because the macro news context indicates supportive, cautiously bullish drivers (OPEC+ extending voluntary production pauses for March 2026, rising geopolitical risk premiums from US military interdictions and tanker seizures, and rising war-risk insurance premiums) which do not satisfy the criteria for structural bearish cycle downward adjustments.
metadata.horizon_rationale: Horizon 10 business days (matching baseline Horizon 14). Adjusted the baseline by narrowing the over-dispersed 80% prediction interval by approximately 45% to a target half-width of 4.10 USD, in accordance with the systematic calibration strategy. Directional downward adjustment was not triggered because the macro news context is cautiously bullish and does not exhibit bearish indicators like demand downgrades or OPEC+ unwind of cuts.

metadata.agent_rationale: Calibrated forecasts as of February 16, 2026. WTI crude oil is classified in an elevated volatility regime (36.1% annualized vol), where short-term geopolitical tensions near the Strait of Hormuz are transitory. Point forecasts are adjusted downward by $1.60 across all horizons to correct for statistical over-forecasting during a structural bearish trend driven by early-2026 tariff shocks (US 15% blanket global tariff) and IEA global demand downgrades (850k bpd). Under our systematic calibration approach, baseline 80% prediction interval widths are narrowed by 30% (5 bd), 45% (10 bd), and 50% (21 bd) to correct baseline over-dispersion and align with the target 80% coverage rate.
metadata.horizon_rationale: Baseline ARIMA point forecast (61.96) is adjusted downward by $1.60 to 60.36 to correct for a persistent statistical over-forecasting bias during structural bearish cycles. Short-term geopolitical premium from the Strait of Hormuz is offset by massive macro headwinds, including Trump's 15% blanket global tariffs (expected to cut oil demand by up to 1 mb/d) and IEA's downgraded demand growth outlook (850k b/d). To correct baseline over-dispersion, the 80% prediction interval is narrowed by 30.0%, producing a calibrated half-width of 3.52 (80% CI: [56.84, 63.88]).

metadata.agent_rationale: WTI prices experienced a sharp geopolitical spike in the week leading to Feb 23, 2026, rising to $66.39 due to Persian Gulf and Iran tensions, classifying the volatility regime as elevated (vol=37.2%). Under our strategy, we treat the pre-computed AutoARIMA baseline as our anchor but perform directional and interval calibration. Point forecasts are adjusted downwards by $1.60 to $1.80 across horizons because temporary geopolitical spikes in elevated volatility regimes tend to fade quickly back toward the underlying bearish supply-demand fundamentals (oversupply projected by the IEA and EIA for 2026). Simultaneously, we narrow the baseline's over-dispersed intervals to meet calibrated 80% coverage targets (target half-widths of 3.65 at 5 bd, 4.10 at 10 bd, and 5.36 at 21 bd).
metadata.horizon_rationale: The volatility regime is classified as elevated (rolling annualised volatility = 37.2%). In mid-February 2026, WTI surged to ~$66.40 from previous levels of ~$60 due to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf and diplomatic risk surrounding Iran. Per our strategy, geopolitical spikes in elevated regimes are temporary and fade quickly. We apply a -$1.60 point adjustment to the AutoARIMA Horizon 7 baseline (66.46 -> 64.86) and systematically narrow the interval half-width by approximately 30% (target half-width 3.65) to correct for baseline over-dispersion and align with the 80% coverage target.

metadata.agent_rationale: Calibrated probabilistic WTI oil price forecast as of March 2, 2026. The volatility regime is classified as 'elevated' (38.6%) following a massive +$4.21 price surge on Monday to close at $71.23, driven by a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and direct US-Iran hostilities. To reflect this new price level, point forecasts are anchored to the Monday close and then adjusted downward ($1.60 at 5-10 bd, $3.00 at 21 bd) to account for the quick fading of geopolitical spikes. Prediction intervals are systematically narrowed (30% at 5 bd, 45% at 10 bd, 50% at 21 bd) to correct the statistical baseline's overestimation of uncertainty.
metadata.horizon_rationale: Point forecast is anchored to the Monday close of $71.23 (+$4.21 from the Friday close of $67.02 due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade and direct US-Iran hostilities), then adjusted downward by $1.60 to account for the systematic fading of geopolitical spikes in elevated volatility regimes. 80% prediction intervals are narrowed by 30% relative to the baseline to correct for systematic overestimation of uncertainty.

metadata.agent_rationale: As of March 9, 2026, WTI crude oil has experienced an extreme upward spike to $90.90, driven by 'Operation Epic Fury' in the Middle East and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran. This represents an acute physical supply threat of up to 8 million bpd. Our rolling 30-day volatility is classified as elevated at 52.5% with an anomalous daily z-score of +3.94. We anchor our point forecasts to the stable AutoARIMA baseline ($91.06, $90.34, and $90.97), as the physical blockade provides robust support for current price levels, meaning no bearish point adjustments are applied. However, we systematically narrow the baseline prediction intervals by 30% (5bd), 45% (10bd), and 50% (21bd) based on our strategy to correct for the baseline's persistent overestimation of uncertainty, aligning our forecasts with the 80% coverage target.
metadata.horizon_rationale: For the 5-business-day horizon (7 calendar days), we anchor to the AutoARIMA point forecast of $91.06. This reflects a consolidation near the recent spike close of $90.90, as shipping lanes adjust to the Strait of Hormuz blockade and the market digests the initial panic of 'Operation Epic Fury'. We systematically narrow the baseline 80% prediction interval width by 30% (target half-width of 3.81 USD vs. the baseline's 5.44 USD) to correct for the statistical model's historical overestimation of price uncertainty, while keeping the distribution centered on the ARIMA anchor.

metadata.agent_rationale: Calibrated probabilistic forecasts as of March 16, 2026. This analysis incorporates real-time geopolitical developments—the outbreak of the 2026 Iran War and closure of the Strait of Hormuz—balanced against the historic 400-million-barrel global emergency oil release. The market is in an extreme volatility regime (vol of 70.8%), but our strategic calibration corrections systematically adjust the AutoARIMA baseline to remove positive point bias and narrow over-expanded intervals to achieve the target 80% coverage across all horizons.
metadata.horizon_rationale: Following WTI's extreme spike to $116 and subsequent correction to $98.71, we classify the market in an extreme volatility regime (annualised vol of 70.8%). The historic global emergency release of 400 million barrels (including 172 million from the US SPR) provides substantial bearish headwinds that offset the Strait of Hormuz blockade. In line with our forecasting strategy, we adjust the AutoARIMA baseline point forecast downward by $1.60 to account for systematic positive bias. To calibrate for the model's tendency to overestimate price uncertainty, we narrow the baseline interval width by 30%, resulting in a calibrated 80% CI half-width of 3.63 (close to our 3.65 target), which is appropriate given high domestic inventory levels capping domestic gains.

metadata.agent_rationale: As of March 23, 2026, the WTI crude oil market is classified under an extreme volatility regime (annualized vol = 71.2%) following joint U.S.-Israeli air strikes on Iran on Feb 28, 2026, and the subsequent de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz (threatening ~20% of global flows). To mitigate this massive shock, a historic 400-million-barrel coordinated SPR release (172 million from the US) has been authorized. The baseline AutoARIMA points at ~$98 represent a highly robust expectation of price consolidation, balancing the massive physical supply deficit against emergency SPR releases. While our strategic priors require narrowing baseline prediction intervals to align with target 80% coverage, doing so fully under extreme vol is highly risky since baseline interval widths are lagging and have not adapted. We therefore apply a tempered 'moderate narrowing' approach (half of the standard adjustment) to maintain healthy uncertainty bands that reflect actual geopolitical risks.
metadata.horizon_rationale: AutoARIMA baseline point forecast of 98.32 (Friday close of 98.32 on March 20, 2026). Given the extreme volatility regime (annualized vol of 71.2%) driven by the Middle East military conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade, we apply a tempered 15% interval narrowing (rather than the standard 30%) to avoid underestimating geopolitical risk while still correcting for systematic baseline over-dispersion.
